gaps.sentence: This new timetable will mean ___ earlier trains.
He apologized for ___ so abrupt in the meeting.
The burglar admitted ___ through the kitchen window.
gaps.explanation: 'Admit' is followed by a gerund: admitted climbing.

gaps.sentence: I was made ___ the dustbin lorry at six in the morning.
gaps.explanation: In the passive, make takes the to-infinitive: was made to wait.

gaps.sentence: I'm looking forward to ___ from you.
gaps.explanation: 'to' is a preposition in look forward to, so -ing follows: hearing.
Negative infinitive: promised not to be late — 'not' goes before 'to'.

gaps.sentence: I look forward to ___ your suggestions at the meeting.
We spent the whole morning ___ for tickets.
gaps.explanation: spend time + -ing: spent the morning queueing.
